newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Global union group asks ILO to stop Korean arrests.
newsitem.headline: Global union group asks ILO to stop Korean arrests.

text.p: A global trade union group asked the International Labour Organisation on Thursday to intervene immediately to prevent South Korea from arresting seven labour leaders who are organising nationwide strikes.

"We have also asked our member organisations to escalate pressure on South Korean representatives in their countries," Luc Demaret, spokesman for the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions (ICFTU), told Reuters.

Korean state prosecutors said on Thursday they were seeking arrest warrants for seven leaders of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions, which is spearheading strikes to protest against new labour legislation.
ICFTU general secretary Bill Jordan asked for ILO intervention in a letter to ILO director-general Michel Hansenne, Demaret said.

He said the group had also decided to extend a mission to Seoul it has planned for later this week. The delegation, which plans to seek meetings with Korean authorities to protest against the new labour legislation, will now be in Seoul from January 11 to 16, Demaret said.
The ICFTU filed a complaint with the ILO in December against Korea's new law, saying it violated internationally recognised trade union rights.

It complained about provisions allowing strikers to be replaced by outside workers, banning dismissed workers from belonging to unions and barring companies from paying strikers during work stoppages.
Demaret said unions would stage protests against Korea on Friday in various cities around the world, including Brussels.
